📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧠 TRADING ROUTINE: YOUR EDGE STARTS BEFORE THE CHART

Most traders lose money before they even open a position. Why? No routine.

Professional traders follow the same daily structure:

- Pre-market review: 30 minutes analyzing overnight moves
- Economic calendar check: knowing what news hits when
- Journal review: what worked yesterday, what didn't
- Trading plan: clear entry zones, stops, targets before markets open

Real example: A trader enters EUR/USD during NFP Friday without checking the calendar. Gets stopped out in 90 seconds by volatility. Cost: 2% account damage that was completely avoidable.

Your routine protects you from impulsive decisions. It creates distance between emotion and execution.

Morning checklist that works:
- Check major indices and currency pairs
- Review your watchlist for setups
- Set alerts, not orders
- Define your risk for the day (max 2-3% total exposure)

PRO TIP: The best traders decide BEFORE the session what they'll trade and what they'll ignore. Everything else is noise.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚖️ CFD VS FUTURES MARGIN: KNOW WHAT YOU'RE TRADING

Both offer leverage. Both can amplify gains and losses. But they work differently.

CFDs (Contracts for Difference):
- Broker sets your leverage (10x to 500x depending on regulation)
- No expiry date, hold positions indefinitely
- Overnight financing costs (swap fees) eat into profits
- You never own the underlying asset

Futures contracts:
- Exchange-determined margin requirements
- Fixed expiry dates (must roll positions)
- No daily financing, just initial and maintenance margin
- Standardized contracts, more transparent pricing

Real scenario: You trade gold CFDs at 100x leverage with 500 dollars. A 1% move against you = account blown. Same position in futures with proper margin might give you breathing room and better cost structure.

Key differences traders miss:
- CFDs have wider spreads during volatility
- Futures have better liquidity in major contracts
- CFDs more flexible for small accounts
- Futures better for serious capital deployment

SMART MONEY RULE: Understand your margin type before sizing positions. CFD leverage is seductive but dangerous. Futures require more capital but offer institutional-grade execution.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 3 DAILY TRADING TIPS

1. WAIT FOR CONFIRMATION
Mid-August typically sees thin liquidity as institutions wind down for summer. Don't chase breakouts. Wait for retest and volume confirmation. False breaks are common in low-volume environments.

2. TRACK CORRELATION CHANGES
Watch Bitcoin and tech stocks correlation this week. When correlation breaks, opportunities emerge. If BTC drops but NASDAQ holds, that divergence tells you something about risk appetite shifting.

3. USE WIDER STOPS IN SUMMER CHOP
Volatility is lower but moves are random. Your normal 20-pip stop might get tagged by noise alone. Consider 1.5x your usual stop distance or reduce position size to maintain same risk.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛡️ CAPITAL PRESERVATION: SURVIVAL BEATS PERFORMANCE

Here's the truth: protecting your account matters more than hitting home runs.

The math is brutal:
- Lose 10%: need 11% to recover
- Lose 25%: need 33% to recover  
- Lose 50%: need 100% to recover
- Lose 75%: need 300% to recover

One bad month can destroy six good ones.

Capital preservation strategies:
- Never risk more than 1-2% per trade
- Cut losing days short (daily loss limit: 3-5%)
- Take partial profits to secure gains
- Step aside when market structure breaks

Example: Trader A makes 5% monthly for 8 months, then loses 30% in one revenge trading session. Net result: still down for the year. Trader B makes steady 2-3% monthly, never loses more than 5% in a month. Compounds consistently.

The defensive mindset:
- Small losses are tuition fees
- Big losses are career enders
- Your goal is staying in the game long enough to catch the big moves
- Preservation first, profit second

PRO TIP: Professional funds often have maximum drawdown limits (10-15%). Once hit, they stop trading and reassess. You should too. Your biggest win is surviving to trade another day.
